card.name: Organizing and integrating information into order
card.fires_on: Words in phrases about organizing, ordering or integrating knowledge or items, such as 'link new information with existing knowledge' or 'placed them in an approximate order'. Mostly non-medical educational or science prose.

modes.label: Linking knowledge
modes.description: Words in a learning-theory sentence about linking new information with existing knowledge.
modes.example: - The successful learner can link new information with<< existing>> knowledge in meaningful ways.

modes.label: Putting things in order
modes.description: Words in phrases about arranging, ordering or making sense of material.
modes.example: "We've identified about 96,000 genes and<< placed>> them in an approximate order.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about sorting, arranging and organizing (Chinese terms for 'return' and 'tidy up', ' sorted', ' frameworks').
card.plain: It fires when the text talks about fitting information together or putting things into order.
